content: 1. Clinical trials have shown that istradefylline at a dose of 40 mg/day increases the peak levels and area under the curve (AUC) of CYP3A4 substrates. However, this effect is not observed with a 20 mg/day dose of istradefylline. 2. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of istradefylline by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Do not exceed 20 mg/day of istradefylline when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 3. Both cobicistat and itraconazole increase each other's levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 4. Itraconazole increases the levels of elvitegravir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 5. Itraconazole significantly increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use of an alternative drug is recommended. 6. Cobicistat significantly increases the levels or effects of ivabradine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 7. Co-administration of ivabradine with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated. 8. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ivacaftor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Reduce the dose of ivacaftor when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Refer to specific product guidelines for precise dosage adjustments. 9. Cobicistat significantly increases the levels or effects of ivosidenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. If co-administration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the ivosidenib dose to 250 mg daily. If the strong inhibitor is discontinued, increase the ivosidenib dose to the recommended 500 mg daily after at least five half-lives of the inhibitor. 10. Ivosidenib decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 11. Avoid co-administration of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates with ivosidenib. If unavoidable, monitor patients for loss of therapeutic efficacy of these drugs. 12. Cobicistat significantly increases the levels or effects of ixabepilone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 13. Co-administration of ixazomib with strong CYP3A inhibitors does not result in clinically meaningful changes in systemic exposure to ixazomib. Monitor closely. 14. Both cobicistat and ketoconazole increase each other's levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 15. Ketoconazole increases the levels of elvitegravir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Ketoconazole significantly increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 17. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of lansoprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Cobicistat significantly increases the levels or effects of lapatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. If co-administration is unavoidable, administer 500 mg lapatinib once daily and increase the dose to the indicated level once cobicistat is discontinued. 19. Larotrectinib increases the levels or effects of elvitegravir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Cobicistat significantly increases the levels or effects of larotrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 21. Cobicistat significantly increases the levels or effects of lefamulin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 22. Avoid co-administration of lefamulin with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 23. Cobicistat significantly increases the levels or effects of lemborexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 24. Avoid co-administration of lemborexant with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors. 25. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of elvitegravir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Lenacapavir, a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor, may increase CYP3A4 substrates initiated within nine months after the last subcutaneous dose of lenacapavir, potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 28. Lenolisib increases the levels or effects of tenofovir AF by inhibiting BCRP transport. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 29. Lenolisib, a BCRP inhibitor, may increase systemic exposure to BCRP substrates. 30. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of lenolisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 31. Cobicistat increases the levels of letermovir by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Tenofovir AF decreases the levels or effects of letermovir by inducing P-glycoprotein (P-gp) efflux transport. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 33. Co-administration of letermovir with P-gp inducers is not recommended. 34. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of levamlodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 35. Co-administration with moderate and strong CYP3A inhibitors increases systemic exposure to amlodipine and may require dose reduction. Monitor for symptoms of hypotension and edema to determine the need for dose adjustment. 36. Both cobicistat and levoketoconazole increase each other's levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 37. Levoketoconazole increases the levels of elvitegravir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Levoketoconazole significantly increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 39. Cobicistat significantly increases the levels or effects of levomilnacipran by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. Do not exceed 80 mg of levomilnacipran daily if co-administration is necessary. 40. Cobicistat significantly increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel intrauterine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 41. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel oral/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma hormone concentrations. Use of a nonhormonal contraceptive is recommended. 42. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of lidocaine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Clinical monitoring is recommended when co-administered with antiarrhythmics. 43. Cobicistat significantly increases the levels or effects of lomitapide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 44. Cobicistat significantly increases the levels or effects of lonafarnib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Lonafarnib is a sensitive CYP3A4 substrate. 45. Lonafarnib increases the levels or effects of tenofovir AF by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (P-gp) transport. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Lonafarnib is a weak P-gp inhibitor. Monitor for adverse reactions if co-administered with P-gp substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious or life-threatening toxicities. Reduce P-gp substrate dose if needed. 46. Lopinavir increases the levels of elvitegravir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Lopinavir/ritonavir significantly increases elvitegravir levels. No data are available to alter current dosing recommendations. The recommended dose is elvitegravir 85 mg orally once daily with lopinavir/ritonavir other than 400/100 mg BID. 48. Lorlatinib decreases the levels or effects of elvitegravir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. 49. Lorlatinib decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of lorlatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 50. Avoid co-administering lorlatinib with strong CYP3A inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the lorlatinib dose by 25 mg/day. If the strong CYP3A inhibitor is discontinued, increase to the previous lorlatinib dose after three plasma half-lives of the strong CYP3A inhibitor. 51. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of losartan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Cobicistat significantly increases the levels or effects of lovastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the potential for serious reactions such as myopathy, including rhabdomyolysis. 53. Elvitegravir may interfere with the manufacturing of lovotibeglogene autotemcel. Discontinue antiretrovirals (ARTs) at least one month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. Some long-acting ARTs may require a longer duration of discontinuation for elimination. 54. Cobicistat increases the levels of lumacaftor/ivacaftor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 55. Due to the induction effect of lumacaftor on CYP3A, at steady-state, the net exposure of ivacaftor is not expected to exceed that when given in the absence of lumacaftor at a dose of 150 mg every 12 hours (the approved dose of ivacaftor monotherapy). Therefore, no dose adjustment is necessary when CYP3A inhibitors are initiated in patients currently taking lumacaftor/ivacaftor. However, when initiating lumacaftor/ivacaftor in patients taking strong CYP3A inhibitors, reduce the dose to one tablet daily (lumacaftor 200 mg/ivacaftor 125 mg total daily dose) for the first week of treatment to allow for the steady-state induction effect of lumacaftor. Following this period, continue with the recommended daily dose. No dose adjustment is required for moderate or weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. 56. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of lumasiran by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 57. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of lumefantrine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Cobicistat significantly increases the levels or effects of lurasidone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the potential for increased systemic exposure of lurasidone, resulting in an increased risk for QT prolongation. 59. Cobicistat significantly increases the levels or effects of lurbinectedin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the lurbinectedin dose by 50%. After the strong CYP3A inhibitor is discontinued for five half-lives, increase lurbinectedin to the dose used before co-administration. 60. Magnesium oxide decreases the levels or effects of elvitegravir by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Separate the dose of elvitegravir from antacids by at least two hours. 61. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Decrease maraviroc dose to 150 mg twice daily when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 62. Cobicistat significantly increases the levels or effects of mavacamten by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the potential for increased systemic exposure of mavacamten, resulting in heart failure due to systolic dysfunction. 63. Mavorixafor increases the levels or effects of tenofovir AF by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (P-gp) transport. Use caution and monitor closely. 64. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of mavorixafor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 65. Cobicistat significantly increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. Avoid co-administration during and for 15 weeks after discontinuing mefloquine. 66. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of methadone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Methadone dose may require adjustment. 67. Elvitegravir decreases the levels of methadone by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Methadone dosage may need to be increased. 68. Cobicistat significantly increases the levels or effects of methylergonovine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the potential for serious and/or life-threatening reactions, such as acute ergot toxicity characterized by peripheral vasospasm and ischemia.
